The schools differ on when it starts and ends — for the pilgrim, Malikis and Shafi'is: from Dhuhr on the {1}th to Fajr on the {2}th; Hanbalis: from Dhuhr on the {3}th to Asr on the {4}th; Hanafis: from Fajr on the {5}th to Asr on the {6}th. No pushing, no arguing — crowd patience is part of the test.

Women wear normal modest dress in ihram — no face veil while in ihram, and in the majority view no gloves (Bukhari {1}; the Hanafis permit them).

Tamattu' and Qiran pilgrims owe a sacrifice (Quran {1}). Buy it as an Adahi voucher through the package or the official Adahi platform before you fly — it is slaughtered in Mina on your behalf; keep the receipt. Ifrad pilgrims owe none.

Hajj is only possible on a permit: through your country's official quota agents or the Nusuk Hajj platform (hajj.nusuk.sa) — never through a "guaranteed visa" on social media. Confirm the booking is in your name, keep the confirmation offline, and note your maktab (camp) number as soon as it is issued.
Whether they come with your package or you book them yourself, check that the flight and hotel dates cover the {1}th–{2}th of Dhul Hijjah plus your travel days, and keep the confirmations offline.
Your group leader knows which one your package follows — Tamattu' is the usual. Pick it here: the steps, duas and checklists follow it.
The Hajj visa comes with the licensed package and is tied to it; a tourist or Umrah visa does not allow Hajj. Check the dates cover the {1}th–{2}th of Dhul Hijjah plus your travel days.
A pilgrimage funded by the pure is more likely to be accepted.
Wind in the courtyard and hours of prostration — an undercap keeps everything in place. A hijab is worn as normal in ihram; only the face veil is left off — and gloves, in the majority view.
The City Sightseeing hop-on hop-off covers Quba, Qiblatayn, Uhud and Baqi' on one ticket ({1}- to {2}-hour passes) — book it from the Places tab.
Proximity means more prayers in congregation — worth every riyal.

Wrap, walk, sit and use the bathroom in it until it feels normal — the number one first-timer anxiety.

Millions of pilgrims from around the world — protect yourself and others. Some pilgrims also need extra vaccines under Saudi MoH rules: polio or yellow fever if travelling from listed countries, and (in {1}) COVID-{2} vaccination or immunity proof for over-{3}s, pregnant women and people with certain chronic illnesses — check the current MoH requirements for your country.

Name, your Saudi-reachable number and hotel on the band; a phone photo of each child in today's clothes makes a description instant if you are separated. Write the group leader's number on paper in the child's pocket every morning too.

Each child needs their own Hajj permit and visa through your licensed package. Saudi Arabia has changed the minimum age for Hajj in recent seasons (children were not allowed in {1}, and the {2} limit changed shortly before Hajj) — confirm the current rule with Nusuk Hajj or your country's Hajj mission before you book.
Paracetamol/ibuprofen in child doses, oral rehydration sachets, plasters, sunscreen (unscented if the child is in ihram).

ACWY vaccination is required by the Saudi Ministry of Health for children too (UK Travel Health Pro gives the age as {1} year or older; check the current MoH rule, and which vaccine suits your child's age, with your clinic) — given at least {2} days before arrival.

Every child needs their own passport with six months' validity from arrival — children's applications can need extra steps in some countries (in-person appointments, both parents' consent), so apply early.
Agree a gate number to meet at after each prayer. Teach them to stay put and ask a uniformed guard, never to wander looking for you. Pack snacks and something familiar for the long waits.

Children need their own visa on Nusuk / through your agent, linked to a parent or guardian on the same booking. A single-entry Umrah visa is cancelled if not used within {1} days of issue, so apply close to travel.

Read Part {1} of the rites — the {2}th to the {3}th — until you can say what happens on each day and which acts are pillars. Then take the Hajj quiz level.

Mina is a city of numbered camps and phones fail in the crowd. Write the maktab number, your camp street and the leader's number on a card and on your wristband — it is how security walks you home if you are lost.
Carry prescriptions; include painkillers, rehydration salts, blister plasters.
